end.summary:
• Applied neutralisation to ant bites, acidic soil, tooth care, antacids and factory waste.
• Correctly identified baking soda and lime as bases used for neutralisation.
• Distinguished neutralising from diluting in the glass example.
• Indicator colour changes remained uncertain; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Khushi practised applying neutralisation to everyday examples and used the idea that a base can neutralise an acid. They correctly explained that adding water only dilutes the acid, while mixing with baking soda can neutralise it. The colour-change explanation was still mixed up and was not fully corrected by the end. At home, use hibiscus or universal-indicator examples to compare dilution with adding a measured amount of base, and ask what each colour means.
